identification.summary: Jasper Sleet is Microsoft's name for North Korea's remote IT worker activity. Microsoft says the workers are mainly focused on making money for the North Korean government [S1]. Operatives use stolen, rented or fabricated identities to get hired into remote IT, software and web development roles. Once hired, they collect salaries that are laundered back to the DPRK and at times steal data or extort their employers [S1]. Microsoft says the workers have used AI since 2024 to scale the operation, and it describes AI use at every stage: getting hired, staying hired and misusing access [S1][S4].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft says it has tracked this global operation since at least early 2020 [S1]. The January 2025 DOJ indictment that Microsoft cites describes fraudulent work from 2018 to 2024 [S1][S6].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Jasper Sleet, formerly tracked as Storm-0287 [S1][S2]. Microsoft tracks other North Korean clusters that use similar fraudulent-employment techniques separately, including Storm-1877 and Moonstone Sleet [S1]. Microsoft has since renamed Storm-1877 to Coral Sleet [S2][S4]. Microsoft's naming mapping lists no other-vendor aliases for Jasper Sleet [S2]. US DOJ actions against the DPRK IT worker scheme do not use Microsoft's cluster names [S5][S6][S7].

attribution.sponsor: Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea). Microsoft says the remote IT workers generate revenue for the North Korean government and likely fall under a particular leadership structure in North Korea [S1].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft attributes the activity to North Korea and attributed at least one 2025 incident response case to Jasper Sleet [S1][S3]. The US government attributes the broader remote IT worker scheme to the DPRK through indictments and guilty pleas, but it does not use the name Jasper Sleet [S5][S6][S7].
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and machine-learning detection of suspect accounts. Microsoft also found a public repository in October 2024 that held suspected workers' photos, resumes, accounts and payment-tracking records [S1]. Microsoft's Incident Response team (DART) investigated a case involving PiKVM devices [S3]. Microsoft also cites DOJ indictments [S1][S6].

objectives: The primary objective is to generate revenue for the DPRK, which Microsoft says violates international sanctions [S1]. Secondary objectives are stealing intellectual property, source code and trade secrets, and extorting employers by threatening to release stolen data [S1]. Microsoft's incident response reporting also cites deploying malicious tools and sending profits to state programs [S3]. In a related DOJ case, workers in the scheme reached ITAR-controlled data at a California defense contractor [S8].

sectors: Information technology and software development (remote roles)
Fortune 500 companies (via staffing and contracting firms)
Defense industrial base (ITAR data exposure in a DOJ case)
regions: Global; Microsoft says targeting has broadened to various industries worldwide [S1]
targeting.notes: The historic focus on US technology, critical manufacturing and transportation companies, and the shift to global targeting, come from Microsoft [S1]. The targeted roles are IT, software development, web development and administrator jobs [S1]. Microsoft says the workers are most often located in North Korea, China and Russia [S1]. The defense-contractor ITAR exposure comes from DOJ case reporting that does not name Jasper Sleet [S8].

capabilities.summary: Identity fraud: personas are stolen, rented from willing people or bought from fraud services, then matched to the target's location. The workers back them with email, GitHub, LinkedIn and freelance-site profiles [S1]. AI: Faceswap is used to place operatives' faces onto stolen ID documents and headshots, and voice-changing software is used in interviews [S1][S4]. Generative AI is used to analyze job postings, build culturally fitting names, polish resumes and keep up job performance [S4]. Facilitators validate identities, open accounts, receive company laptops and run laptop farms [S1]. Remote access: IP-based KVM devices (PiKVM, TinyPilot) and RMM tools (JumpConnect, RustDesk, TeamViewer, AnyViewer, AnyDesk) [S1]. Microsoft DART observed PiKVM used as an out-of-band channel that bypassed EDR and exfiltrated data [S3]. Evasion: VPNs (notably Astrill VPN), VPSs and proxies; workers also avoid turning on cameras [S1].

campaigns.name: Microsoft begins tracking the remote IT worker operation
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says it has tracked the global operation since at least early 2020. US government reporting it cites found more than 300 US companies unknowingly employed these workers between 2020 and 2022.

campaigns.name: Public repository exposure
campaigns.summary: Microsoft found a public repository with photos of suspected workers, resumes, email accounts, wallet information and payment-tracking sheets.

campaigns.name: DOJ indictment of Jin Sung-Il, Pak Jin-Song and three facilitators
campaigns.summary: Two North Korean nationals and three facilitators were charged over work obtained from at least 64 US companies between 2018 and 2024. Payments from ten of those companies totaled at least $866,255. Microsoft cites this case in its Jasper Sleet reporting.

campaigns.name: Microsoft disruption and DOJ coordinated nationwide actions
campaigns.summary: Microsoft published its Jasper Sleet profile and suspended 3,000 known Outlook/Hotmail accounts created by North Korean IT workers. The same day, DOJ announced an arrest, two indictments, searches of 29 suspected laptop farms in 16 states, and seizures of 29 financial accounts and 21 websites. DOJ says the schemes involved more than 100 US companies. The DOJ materials do not use the Jasper Sleet name.

campaigns.name: Five facilitators plead guilty
campaigns.summary: DOJ announced guilty pleas from five facilitators in schemes that affected more than 136 US companies and generated over $2.2 million for the DPRK. The cluster is not named.

campaigns.name: DART PiKVM incident response
campaigns.summary: Microsoft DART traced four compromised accounts that connected PiKVM devices to employer workstations, which led to data exfiltration, to Jasper Sleet.

campaigns.name: AI-as-tradecraft reporting
campaigns.summary: Microsoft describes Jasper Sleet using AI across the lifecycle to get hired, stay hired and misuse access. Microsoft says it has disrupted thousands of accounts linked to fraudulent IT worker activity.

diamond.adversary: DPRK remote IT workers, most often located in North Korea, China and Russia, supported by willing facilitators in the US and elsewhere [S1][S5].
diamond.capability: Identity fraud enhanced by AI (Faceswap, voice changers, generative AI for resumes and job analysis); facilitator-run laptop farms; KVM devices and RMM tools; data theft and extortion [S1][S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Facilitator-hosted company laptops; PiKVM and TinyPilot devices; Astrill VPN, VPSs and proxies; consumer Outlook/Hotmail accounts; GitHub, LinkedIn and freelance profiles; and facilitator bank accounts used for laundering [S1][S3].
diamond.victim: Organizations hiring remote IT and software staff. The historic focus was US technology, critical manufacturing and transportation, and targeting has since gone global [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Sanctions evasion and revenue generation for the DPRK government [S1].
diamond.technology: Remote-hiring and onboarding processes, staffing and contracting intermediaries, and the legitimate credentials issued to new hires [S1][S3][S4].

gaps: No MITRE ATT&CK group ID is recorded for Jasper Sleet, and Microsoft's naming mapping lists no other-vendor aliases [S2]. Mappings to other vendors' DPRK IT worker clusters were not confirmed by any cited source, so none are added.

Cluster boundaries are unclear. Microsoft says Storm-1877 (now Coral Sleet) and Moonstone Sleet use similar fraudulent-employment techniques, but it does not publicly explain how it separates them from Jasper Sleet [S1][S4].
The DOJ indictments and pleas cover the DPRK IT worker scheme but do not use Microsoft's names. Which defendants map to Jasper Sleet rather than other clusters is not established [S5][S6][S7].

Date discrepancy: Microsoft dates the indictment of two North Korean nationals and three facilitators to January 3, 2025, while press coverage reported the announcement on January 23-24, 2025 [S1][S6].
The DOJ primary documents on justice.gov could not be opened. Details come from search summaries and press coverage [S5][S6][S7][S8].
The total number of operatives, total revenue attributable to Jasper Sleet, and victim identities in the PiKVM incident are not public [S1][S3].

The publication date of Microsoft's 'Imposter for hire' post (S3), given here as December 11, 2025, could not be confirmed from search results; the post's content (four accounts tied to PiKVM devices, traced to Jasper Sleet) was confirmed [S3].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the hiring and onboarding pipeline (staffing firms, contractors, freelance platforms), identity systems (Entra ID) and remote-access paths into developer and administrator workstations [S1][S3]. STEP 2: Remote work and contractor-heavy staffing at DIB and IT support providers widen the attack surface. Insider-type access bypasses perimeter defenses, and KVM hardware bypasses EDR [S1][S3][S8]. STEP 3: The doctrinal template is fabricated persona, AI-assisted interview, hire, facilitator laptop farm with KVM or RMM, and long-term access. Payroll is laundered to the DPRK, with optional data theft or extortion [S1][S4]. STEP 4: The MLCOA is revenue generation from remote IT jobs at US and allied firms [S1]. The MDCOA is a placed worker at a defense contractor or DoD IT provider stealing ITAR or source-code data, or handing access to other DPRK operators [S1][S3][S8]. Candidate indicators: impossible or atypical travel sign-ins involving China or Russia; Astrill VPN egress; unsanctioned RMM tools (AnyDesk, RustDesk, TeamViewer); PiKVM or TinyPilot devices on endpoints; new hires who avoid cameras; and personas reused across employers [S1][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: combine HR and contractor-vetting data with identity telemetry, such as Microsoft's 'Sign-in activity by a suspected North Korean entity Jasper Sleet' alert, so insider-risk cases appear in the cyber picture [S1][S4]. (2) Authorities: most activity is fraud and sanctions evasion handled by DOJ and FBI. Any cyber response on contractor networks requires law enforcement and counterintelligence coordination, and Microsoft advises not tipping off suspects [S1][S5]. (3) Mission assurance: enforce least privilege and RMM and KVM controls for remote developers and administrators on DoD-adjacent contracts, because an ITAR exposure has already occurred [S1][S3][S8]. (4) Coordination: work with DC3, the DIB CS program and staffing vendors on identity verification and on sharing persona indicators.
